To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the simultaneous expression of stress responsive TF, AtDRE2A, AtABF3 and AtHB7, improves salinity and drought tolerance in peanut (Arachishypogaea) by enhancing cellular tolerance to desiccation and water use efficiency.

simultaneous expression of abiotic stress-responsive transcription factors, AtDRE2B1, AtHB7, and AtABF, in peanut (Arachishypogaea L.) improves salinity and drought tolerance by enhancing reactive oxygen species scavengers, osmotic adjustment, and expression of various cell tolerance genes.
co-expression of three transcription factors AtDREB, AtHB7, and AtABF in peanut improved drought tolerance by inducing expression of various stress-responsive genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the drought tolerance of peanut by over-expressing stress responsive transcription factors.
the development of transgenic peanut lines with simultaneous expression of stress-responsive transcription factors, AtDREBA2A, AtABF3 and AtHB7, to improve drought and salinity tolerance.

the development of transgenic peanut (Arachishypogaea L.) plants expressing stress responsive transcription factors, DREB2A (AtDREB2), HB7 (AtHB7) and ABF3 (AtABF3) to impart tolerance to drought, salt stress and oxidative stress.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the co-expression of three transcription factors (AtDREB2, AtHB7, AtABF3) improved drought and salinity tolerance in peanut.
co-expression of AtDREB, AtHB7, and AtABF TFs improved drought tolerance in peanut.

the simultaneous expression of three transcription factors AtDREB1A, AtHB and AtABF in transgenic peanut plants enhanced the drought and salt stress tolerance in transgenics by activating multiple tolerance mechanisms and the strategy can be employed for improving abiotic stress tolerance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a transgenic peanut plant that is tolerant to drought, salinities and oxidative stresses.
we have identified three stress responsive transcription factors that are involved in the activation of multiple downstream genes that are involved in cellular tolerance to desiccation.
we have identified the genes that can help in improving abiotic stress tolerance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
co-expression of multiple transcription factors involved in downstream gene expression is a promising strategy for improving abiotic stress tolerance.
the simultaneous expression of stress responsive TF can activate multiple CT pathway, which can be employed to develop stress tolerant crop plants.
the expression of multiple TFs in a crop plant can lead to improved stress tolerance.
